notes_list.title: Electrophilic Addition to Alkenes
notes_list.basic_overview: Alkenes react with electrophiles because the π bond is electron-rich. The pathway may involve a carbocation or a bridged intermediate depending on reagent.
notes_list.extra_info_content: Mechanistic identity determines regio- and stereochemistry. HX often proceeds through carbocation-like intermediate; halogenation proceeds through a halonium ion and gives anti addition.
notes_list.examples: HBr addition, Br2 addition, acid-catalyzed hydration and halohydrin formation.
notes_list.conditions_and_medium: Nonpolar solvents such as CCl4 historically used for halogenation; water/alcohol can trap halonium ions. Strong acid used for acid hydration.
notes_list.mechanism_steps: 1. π bond attacks electrophile. 2. Intermediate forms. 3. Nucleophile attacks. 4. Proton transfer/workup. Check rearrangement and stereochemistry.
notes_list.kinetics_and_energy: Rate depends on electrophile formation and alkene nucleophilicity; substituents alter intermediate and transition-state stability.
notes_list.selectivity_and_stereochemistry: Central framework for alkene reaction prediction.
notes_list.common_traps: Markovnikov orientation is not a universal rule; hydroboration gives anti-Markovnikov alcohols, while halogenation is governed by halonium geometry.

exam_focus.level: IIT-JAM / MSc entrance / GATE concept depth
